title: Google Research Scaling Transformer Inference Efficiency: 2D/3D Mesh Sharding Rules, Prefix-Shared KV Slices & Decode Layout
author: repo-triad-forge

edges.description: Subproject scaling_transformer_inference_efficiency in snapshot google-research-master (archive snapshot, non-git); arXiv:2211.05102
Prefix-shared batch decoding (batch % prefix_batch == 0) reduces KV memory traffic when sampling multiple self-consistency reasoning traces per prompt

claims.assertion: partitioning.py separates logical tensor dimensions from physical 3D TPU mesh axes (x, y, z) using make_rules_two_d, make_rules_one_d, make_rules_weight_gathered, AttnAllToAll collective modes, and thread-local PartitioningRules context scoping.

inference.py infer() shares prefix KV caches across multi-sample decode batches (batch % prefix_batch == 0), pre-slices RoPE sin/cos tables once per prefix via lax.dynamic_slice_in_dim + vmap, and performs in-place static KV buffer updates with lax.dynamic_update_index_in_dim.

distilled_learning: Decouple logical tensor partitioning rules from physical device meshes and share prompt-prefix KV caches (batch % prefix_batch == 0) when generating multiple continuation samples.
